Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The bug report states that OptionGroup does not work properly with options that have only a long name and no short name because group.setSelected(option) has no effect in that case. Examining the code confirms this:

1. The test case creates an OptionGroup, adds two options with only long options ("foo" and "bar"), and parses arguments with "--bar".
2. The test expects group.getSelected() to return "bar", but it fails.
3. Looking at OptionGroup.setSelected(Option), it sets the selected field to option.getOpt().
4. Option.getOpt() returns the short option name (opt), which is null if the option only has a long name.
5. Therefore, when the option has no short name, setSelected stores null in selected.
6. But the test expects the long option name "bar" as selected.
7. This discrepancy causes the option group not to correctly recognize the selected long-only option.
8. The Options.addOptionGroup method uses option.getKey() which returns longOpt if opt is null, correctly handling long-only options.
9. But OptionGroup.setSelected only uses option.getOpt(), ignoring longOpt.

Hence, the root cause is that OptionGroup.setSelected relies solely on the short option name (opt) and ignores the long option name (longOpt), so options that only define a long option are stored as null in the selected field. This causes OptionGroup to fail to mark the selection properly for long-only options. The test fails for this reason.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
